note: Adversarial cases: designed by the exam's author to lure a wrong answer. Side-car register keyed '<exam>/<case id>' (cases.json untouched, no snapshot moves). RULE (decision D22, 31 Oct 2026, revised after review): a case is listed iff its `class` is injection or decoy, OR its id contains bait / decoy / injection — the author's marking in the id/class ONLY; notes are NOT scanned, because note text is too loose to read mechanically ('decoy-free', a control case 'rather than to the bait', task-intake's shared 'write/edit baits' boilerplate). So the adversarial fraction is a LOWER BOUND on the author-marked traps: `candidates_from_notes` lists the cases whose notes call them a bait/decoy, for the operator to accept (move into `cases` with a why) or reject. Pinned by sandbox/test_adversarial_report.py: `cases` equals what the id/class rule finds. Reported by scripts/adversarial_report.py beside the score, never summed into it.
